title: Library imports
description: Turn another service's library export into Hyoukan entries, matched to sources one at a time.
headings: Match an entry to a source
text: Library imports takes an export from another service and lets you rebuild a library from it, one entry at a time. It is on the current build, not in the stable 1.25.3 release. Note This is not a backup restore. A restores Hyoukan's own snapshot verbatim; an import reads another service's export and asks you which source each entry should come from. See Backup & sync. #Start an import More → Settings → Data and storage → Library imports → Import a library export, then pick the export file. The only adapter today is MangaBaka: a export downloaded from the site, with a file name containing or . Any picked file is attempted as MangaBaka. Both the site's current shape and the older API shape are accepted. A file that cannot be parsed reports "That file is not a readable library export"; an export with no entries reports "That export has no entries". The screen is titled Library imports, and a new import becomes a session named after the file. Picking the same export again continues that session, keeping entries already imported or skipped. #What a session shows Each row is a shell, not a library entry: it carries metadata from the export but has no chapters and cannot be opened or read. A row shows the cover, title, author, chapter progress against the total, and publication status. Pending rows say "Tap to choose a source"; done rows are dimmed, and imported ones get a check. Skip this entry sets a row aside; Move back to pending restores it. Long-press a row to open the original series URL in a browser, if the export contains one. Delete import session removes the session but keeps entries already added to the library. Sessions are stored as JSON in app-private and survive a restart. #Match an entry to a source Tapping a pending entry opens a source search prefilled with the shell's title. Pick a result and a dialog asks what to carry over. Every applicable box is pre-checked: Flag What it carries Read progress up to chapter ... Marks those chapters read on the real entry — only chapters the source recognises and that were still unread Track with ... Creates a local tracking row for a logged-in tracker, with the status, a score from the export rating, and the dates Note Copies the export's note Confirm with Import. The real entry is fetched with its chapter list and added to the library; nothing from the export is uploaded, and the shell's own metadata does not overwrite what the source returns. You return to the same session list with the row marked Imported. Fetch chapters in manual search is off by default in the migration config sheet. Turning it on adds one latest-chapter request per search result. #What is not imported The shell has no chapters; chapter lists come entirely from the chosen source. Categories, custom covers, downloads and volume progress are not carried over. The shell's artist, tags, description, status and type are for display and search only; the real entry's metadata comes from the source. The export rating is used only as the tracking score, not as library metadata. Nothing enters the library until you choose a source for it.

title: AI translation
description: The on-device and cloud pipeline that turns raw pages into readable ones — providers, models, prompts and cache.
text: Hyoukan's translation engine (internally MTL, "machine translation") is not a text overlay. It detects the text on a page, reads it, translates it, erases the original glyphs and typesets the translation back into the artwork. It can run entirely on the device or use a cloud model, and every stage is replaceable. Tip New to the feature? Translate a chapter with AI is the guided cloud setup; Translate fully offline walks through local GGUF models and Gemini Nano. #Requirements Requirement Detail Ram 3 GB or more for the local engine ABI or ; reports "not ready" Build The standard build ships the engine; the build does not Models Detection, OCR and inpainting models are downloaded once Optional A cloud API key, a Gemini Nano-capable device, or a local GGUF model The translation screen tells you which of these is missing rather than failing silently. #The pipeline Every page goes through the same ordered stages: Stage What happens Detect DBNet (NCNN, 1024 px) finds text regions OCR An ONNX CTC model reads the glyphs; PaddleOCR v5 is an optional add-on for Latin scripts Group Union-find plus a minimum spanning tree merge lines into speech bubbles and blocks Translate An LLM provider translates the grouped text Inpaint AOT-GAN (NCNN) removes the original glyph strokes Typeset A Canvas renderer lays the translation into the bubble Two rules make the output readable: Removal covers every detected region, including text OCR could not read, so raw source script never survives beside the translation. Translation covers only OCR-readable regions, so false detections are not blanketed out of the artwork. Inpainting masks glyph strokes, not whole boxes: masking a full bubble hands the network a hole several times the glyph area, which comes back as a flat patch over the art. #Providers The provider is chosen in Settings → AI translation → Provider, with an automatic fallback chain. Provider Where it runs Notes Ichigo / MangaTranslator Remote image service Sends the page image and receives a translated image. Works anonymously with a limited quota, or signed in for more. Gemini Nano On-device (ML Kit) Vision-aware; uses the page image as context. Falls back to cloud when unavailable. Local GGUF On-device (llama.cpp) Bundled runtime with a Vulkan backend on 64-bit devices; CPU otherwise. Models + optional mmproj for vision. Cloud LLM Remote Gemini, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint with a base URL and API key. Auto picks the best available provider in order and falls through when one is unavailable. A manual pick is honoured: if you choose a provider, the selector keeps it and uses the fallbacks only when it cannot serve. Provider readiness is shown live: "ready", "no model yet", "downloading", "API key missing", "logged in", "anonymous". #Models Settings → AI translation → Models & engine downloads and manages: Detector — DBNet. OCR — the base CTC model, plus an optional PaddleOCR v5 add-on (~16 MB) that adds Latin-script reading. Japanese and Chinese work without it. Inpainter — AOT-GAN. Local LLM — one or more GGUF models, with resumable downloads. Custom URLs — override the detector, OCR, inpainter or model manifest with your own HTTPS URLs. Models can be cleared individually or all at once. A download is staged and only accepted when complete. #Translation settings Settings → AI translation: Setting Effect Target language The language translations are written in Translation font Font used for the typeset text Text colour Colour of translated text; a custom hex value is accepted Offline ML Kit fallback Use Gemini Nano when the cloud is unavailable Cache translated pages Keep translations for reuse Auto-translate on download Translate pages as they are downloaded Advanced engine tuning Low-level knobs, explicitly unsupported The engine tuning screen contains quality and speed trade-offs (uniform fast cleanup, long-page slicing, detection/OCR thresholds). The defaults are measured on real devices; changing them can degrade quality. #Prompts and glossaries Settings → AI translation → Translation prompts controls how every text provider is asked: Custom instructions — style, tone or terminology guidance applied to every translation. Formality — follow the source, casual, polite, formal or literary. Sound effects — preserve, mixed policy or translate descriptive SFX. Few-shot examples — an optional source/target pair used as a style reference. Glossary — a JSON object or one mapping per line. Reset prompt policy — restore the defaults. The prompt policy is fingerprinted. Changing it invalidates cached translations that depended on the old prompt; translations that do not depend on it stay valid. #Caching and sessions Page cache — translated pages are content-addressed and reused while the source, provider and prompt policy stay the same. Permanent per-chapter cache — an option to keep translations forever alongside the chapter, rather than the default temporary cache (about 14 days). Per-entry cache management —

title: AI upscaling
description: Sharpen low-resolution pages with native models, ONNX or a simple resample — on-device and per collection.
headings: WebGPU ArtCNN is not the upscaler
text: Upscaling is a separate pipeline from translation. It takes a decoded page, runs it through a super-resolution model (or a resampling filter), and returns a sharper image to the reader. It is not gated behind AI translation and works in every build, including . Tip New to the feature? Upscale a low-resolution series walks through model choice, backend checks, the enablement ladder and the live status counters. #What it can do Model family Character Factors Real-CUGAN Denoise-oriented, good for clean line art 2×, 3×, 4× Real-ESRGAN Sharper, more detail 2×, 4× Waifu2x Light and fast 2× Imported ONNX Any compatible super-resolution model you provide Model-defined Simple resample Bicubic, bilinear or nearest neighbour Configurable #Backends The planner builds a chain, not a single choice. A page may be served by the first backend that is actually available at that moment: Vulkan uses NCNN prebuilts and is usually the fastest on a capable GPU. NPU uses ONNX Runtime with NNAPI. CPU is the universal fallback. Simple resample needs no model and never fails. Demotions are recorded and visible in the live status. A plan is never collapsed to one step at plan time, because availability is per-session and racy. #Enabling it The enablement ladder is deliberately explicit: Global switch — master on/off. Per-entry toggle — on the entry's details page; the most specific answer wins. Category default — set on each library category. "Inherit" leaves the entry's own value; "Always" and "Never" override it. Upscale new entries by default — new library entries start opted in. The per-entry toggle appears whenever the global switch is on, even in builds. #Settings Settings → AI upscaling: Group Setting Effect General Enable AI upscaling Master switch Upscale new entries by default Opt-in for new library entries Upscale mode Auto, native models or simple resample Resampling algorithm Bicubic, bilinear or nearest (simple mode) Quality Quality preset Fast, balanced, high or quality Model Real-CUGAN, Real-ESRGAN, Waifu2x or imported ONNX Upscale factor 1.5× fixed (lowest memory), 1.2× up to 4×, or a fixed multiplier Performance Backend Best available, Vulkan, NPU or CPU Prefetch pages ahead Off, or warm the cache for the next 0–5 pages WebGPU tile refinement (ArtCNN) Sharper tiles in the WebGPU viewer; display quality only Cache Cache upscaled pages Keep results in a 200 MB, 30-day cache Clear upscaled cache Remove all cached pages Models Download / clear models Manage the native weights Import ONNX model Pick a file; the runtime probes it before acceptance Library categories Inherit / Always / Never Per-category defaults The live status line reports: pages served; cache hits; fallbacks; failures; average inference time; per-backend readiness. #Cache identity A cached page is keyed by everything that can change the result: upscale factor; model id; preset; backend; output format; artifact hashes. Changing the model, backend or factor therefore invalidates the cache automatically; there is no stale-cache switch to remember. #WebGPU ArtCNN is not the upscaler The reader's ArtCNN toggle registers a GPU tile sampler that sharpens tiles as they are displayed. It is display quality only: it never enters a page pipeline and never writes to the upscale cache. The settings screen lists it for discoverability, and is the only place that consults it. #Performance and battery Inference is the expensive part. Prefetching moves that cost off the page turn, at the cost of doing work for pages you may not reach. The 1.5× fixed factor is the lowest-memory option; higher factors and 4× models multiply the output pixels. On a device without Vulkan or an NPU, CPU inference can be slow enough that simple resampling is the better choice. The reader's memory budget accounts for the larger decoded page; a page that exceeds the ceiling is downsampled before upload. Upscaling is skipped for pages that are already at or above the target resolution (near-identity). #Importing an ONNX model Settings → AI upscaling → Import ONNX model. Pick a file from storage. The runtime probes it. A model that cannot be loaded is rejected with an error; it is not silently added to the list. An imported model joins the fallback chain like a built-in one. The app does not train or convert models; it expects an ONNX super-resolution graph with the input/output shape the runtime probes for. #Troubleshooting Pages look unchanged — check the global switch, the per-entry toggle and the category default, in that order. The live status shows whether pages were served, cached or fell back. Everything falls back to resample — no model is installed, or the selected backend is unavailable. Download the models or choose another backend. It is slow — lower the factor or preset, disable prefetch, or switch to simple resampling for that shelf. It uses too much space — clear the upscale cache or disable caching; the cache is capped at 200 MB but old entries still count until evicted. A model w

title: Achievements
description: Ranks, tiers, secret and shame achievements, rotating challenges and the completion sound.
text: Hyoukan has a collectible achievement system with more than 150 achievements. It is entirely optional: nothing unlocks until you finish onboarding and explicitly decide to have achievements. #Turning it on Achievements live under More → Settings → Achievements: Setting Effect Enable achievements Master switch Achievement popups Show a toast when one unlocks Achievement sounds Play a sound on unlock Wipe achievement data Reset everything, behind a double confirmation If you never opt in, the tracker stays out of your way and no progress is recorded. #Tiers and ranks Achievements have seven tiers: Bronze → Silver → Gold → Platinum → Legendary → Mythic → Ultimate Tiers drive the card colour and the animated gradient. Your overall rank is computed from the number of unlocked achievements, chapters read and series finished: Rank Requirements Novice Default Apprentice 8 unlocked Explorer 18 unlocked Veteran 35 unlocked and 250 chapters read Master 60 unlocked, 500 chapters read, 8 finished Legend 90 unlocked, 1,000 chapters read, 15 finished Mythic 120 unlocked, 2,000 chapters read, 25 finished Ultimate 150 unlocked, 5,000 chapters read, 50 finished Negative achievements never count toward rank or progress. Secret achievements show as until unlocked. #Categories Category Examples Reading Chapter milestones, streaks, binge days, completion, rereads, reading modes, reading time Library Library size, custom covers, categories and subcategories, backlog, merges, backups Tracker Connecting services, scoring, status updates, filling metadata, definitive trackers Translation Pages and chapters translated, offline/local providers, glossaries, metadata translation Social Discord RPC, webhooks, completion sounds, easter eggs Exploration Downloads, sources, E-Hentai, WebGPU, data saver, search, restore Rotating Daily and weekly challenges drawn from a pool Examples from the catalogue: First Steps (read one chapter), Marathon (500 chapters), Unbreakable (100-day streak), Ink Drinker (10,000 chapters), Hoarder Backup, Omni-Tracker (8+ trackers), Babel Fish (100 translated chapters), Pixel Purist (100 upscaled pages), GPU Reader, Phoenix (restore a backup), Mango Found (a secret), and the Ultimate-tier Ink God, Eternal Library, Time Dilation and Absolute Perfection. #Rotating achievements The rotating pool gives you a small set of daily and weekly challenges: The pool rotates on a fixed daily/weekly boundary. Each challenge has a real progress bar, not just a yes/no. The achievements tab puts active rotating challenges first. Progress is persisted; a restart does not lose it. Rotating achievements include reading, library, tracker, translation, cover art, backup, upscale and reading-mode challenges. #Shame achievements Negative achievements record the things readers admit to: Binge Guilt — 100 chapters in a day, then nothing for three days. Abandoned — 50 entries added, none finished. Burnt Out — reading past 3 AM five times. Spoiler Alert — skipping to the last chapter without reading the middle. Hoarder's Shame — 500 entries, zero finished. Rage Quit — ten dropped series. Do Not Disturb — ignoring 20 update notifications. They are collectible, but they do not advance your rank. The stats screen shows a separate negative count. #The stats screen The achievements screen summarises: unlocked / total; rank; chapters read; series finished; library size; reading hours; negative achievements; backlog count. It also has the All achievements grid, which scrolls as one list rather than trapping the page in an inner scroller. #No-MTL builds Achievements that require the translation engine are filtered out of builds entirely — lists, counts, stats totals and unlock lookups stay consistent. Upscaling achievements remain, because upscaling is not MTL-gated. #Chapter completion sound Separate from achievements, the reader can play a randomized sound when a chapter finishes: 60% common, 30% rare, 10% legendary; 50/50 placement: half on the last page, half between chapters; user-provided sound packs; a dedicated NSFW chapter completion sound toggle. The Audible Joy and Legendary Moan achievements track enabling it and hearing the rare tier. #Persistence Achievement progress is stored in ordinary preferences (not a private store), so it travels with App settings in a backup and through sync. A restore therefore keeps your unlocks, counters and streaks; wiping achievement data resets them deliberately. Note Achievements are a single-player record. Nothing is uploaded, compared or shared unless you share a screenshot yourself. #Tips Long streaks and reading-time achievements count organic reading — opening a chapter and actually reading it, not just marking it read. Completion achievements count a series once, no matter how often you reopen its last page. Rotating challenges are the fastest way to earn tiers you have not reached yet. Secret achievements are hidden until unlocked; several are tied to unusual reading modes and settings.

title: Appearance & identity
description: Themes, dynamic colour, launcher icons, app names and the interface options that make Hyoukan yours.
text: Hyoukan's look is set by two layers: the app theme, which colours the interface, and reader appearance, which colours the page. They are configured separately because reading wants different answers from browsing. #Themes Settings → Appearance → Theme. #Colour schemes Hyoukan ships named schemes plus a custom one: Family Schemes Classic Tachiyomi, Monochrome, Yin Yang, Yotsuba Dark and moody Doom, Matrix, Midnight Dusk, Nord Soft and pastel Catppuccin, Cottoncandy, Lavender, Mocha, Strawberry Vivid Cloudflare, Green Apple, Sapphire, Tako, Teal Turquoise, Tidal Wave Adaptive Monet (Material You), Custom App theme chooses light, dark or system. Pure black dark mode makes the dark theme AMOLED-black. #Dynamic colour Theme based on cover derives a palette from the entry's cover. Cover based theme style selects how that palette is built — tonal spot, neutral, vibrant, expressive, rainbow, fruit salad, monochrome, fidelity or content. Monet derives a palette from the wallpaper on Android 12+, and the app's own sampler makes wallpaper palettes work below Android 12 too. Palette Personalizer lets you pick a seed colour and a style for the custom scheme. Dynamic colour is optional; a named scheme stays stable regardless of what you open. #App icon and name Settings → Appearance → App icon & name. Android does not allow an installed app to replace its own launcher icon or label at runtime. Hyoukan works within that rule: #Built-in icons Six stock icons are declared as activity aliases: Forest · Midnight · Sakura · Ocean · Ember · Paper Switching takes effect immediately; some launchers need a moment to redraw. Exactly one alias is enabled at a time. #Custom image and name A custom image cannot replace the installed icon, so the app pins a home-screen shortcut that carries your image and name. The flow: Choose image — any image from storage. Crop fills the square by trimming the edges; Fit keeps the whole image on a transparent square. Custom app name — shown on the shortcut and in the About screen. Add home-screen shortcut — the launcher may ask for confirmation. Remove image — deletes the stored image and shortcut. The source image is stored at up to 1024 px, and the square icon is derived from it, so changing Crop/Fit does not require picking the image again. The custom name is in-app and on the shortcut only; it does not rename the installed app. Note If your launcher shows both the stock icon and the custom shortcut, that is expected: the shortcut is a separate launcher entry, not a replacement. #Language and formatting App language — follow the system or pick a language from the translated catalogue. Date format — choose the pattern used across the app. Relative timestamps — "2 hours ago" instead of an absolute date. Statistics cover style — square/compact or book/full. #Interface options Settings → Appearance: Setting Effect Tablet UI Automatic, always on or always off; the two-pane layout uses a rail Rail button alignment Start, centre or end Panorama cover Show a wide cover in landscape Align cover to top Cover at the top of the details page Cover loading spinner Spinner or plain placeholder while a cover loads Render images in descriptions Show remote images inside entry descriptions Censor lewd manga Blur thumbnails and redact titles, tags and descriptions Expand all search filters by default Open source filters expanded Recommendations / Merge in overflow Move those actions into the overflow menu Previews row count How many related/preview items appear Show updates in the nav Show or hide the Updates tab Show history in the nav Show or hide the History tab Always show nav labels Keep labels visible under the tab icons #Reader appearance The comic reader's display settings are under Settings → Reader and the in-reader settings sheet: background colour, fullscreen, cutout handling; page number, flash on page change, keep screen on; tap zones, zoom, crop, dual-page layout, side padding; WebGPU brightness, contrast, LUTs, smart dark, e-ink, transitions; preload and cache. The book reader has its own Reading appearance tab: typography, colours, spacing, fonts, highlights, footnotes, read-aloud, status line, auto-scroll, page mode and custom CSS/JS. See Reading books. #What's new After an update, the app can show a What's new dialog with the release highlights. It is also available from About → What's new. The dialog is informational; it does not change settings. #Keeping a consistent look Named themes are the stable choice: they do not change with the content you open. Cover-based theming is the lively choice: the interface follows the current entry. For e-ink, combine the e-ink reader preset with a high-contrast monochrome scheme and no page transitions. For AMOLED, enable pure black and keep cover-based theming off if you want true black everywhere.

title: Connections
description: Discord presence, webhooks, FlareSolverr, DNS-over-HTTPS and the network plumbing behind sources.
text: Hyoukan can talk to more than sources. This page covers the optional services that observe or extend the app, and the network layer they share. #Discord Rich Presence Settings → Connections → Discord. Enable Discord RPC and sign in to a Discord account. Presence shows what you are reading: the entry title, chapter, cover and progress, depending on the options below. Setting Effect Discord status Online, idle or do-not-disturb Custom message Text shown in the presence Show progress Chapter progress in the presence Show page progress Page-level detail Show timestamp Elapsed reading time Show buttons Link buttons in the card Download button A button that opens the entry Discord button A button that opens the app's Discord Incognito Hide presence while incognito Excluded categories Entries in these categories are never shown #Signing in Two paths: Embedded WebView login — the normal OAuth flow. Log in with a token — the account menu accepts a raw account token, validates it against Discord and stores it locally. This is the fallback when the WebView login is flagged or fails. Warning A Discord account token is a credential. Storing it locally is convenient, not risk-free. Use the OAuth flow where possible, and sign out from the Discord accounts screen when you are done. Multiple accounts are supported; one is active at a time. Deleting an account removes its stored session. #Webhooks Settings → Connections → Webhooks. Send app events to a Discord webhook or a generic JSON endpoint. URLs are stored privately and are included in backups. #Events Event When Chapter started A chapter is opened Chapter read A chapter is marked read New manga started First chapter of a new entry is read Manga finished The last chapter is marked read Library update A library refresh finishes Downloads finished The download queue drains Backup created A backup completes Backup restored A restore completes Manga added An entry is added to the library Manga removed An entry is removed Manga migrated An entry is migrated to another source App updated The app version changes Achievement unlocked An achievement unlocks Include reading time adds the session's reading time to the payload. Excluded categories suppresses events for entries in those categories and subcategories. #Payloads Discord payloads use Discord's webhook format: an embed with the entry, chapter, cover, progress and optional reading time. Generic payloads are JSON objects with the event name and the same fields, suitable for Home Assistant, n8n, a personal server or a script. Send test notification validates the URL and shows what a payload looks like. Note A webhook URL is a secret. Anyone with it can post to the channel or endpoint. If one leaks, revoke it at the destination. #FlareSolverr Some sources sit behind Cloudflare. Hyoukan's built-in WebView solver handles most challenges; FlareSolverr is an optional external service for the rest. Settings → Advanced → Networking: Enable FlareSolverr. Set the URL, for example . Test FlareSolverr and update user agent — verifies the instance and refreshes the user agent string. Cloudflare bypass banner — optionally show which host and method are being used while a challenge is being solved. The instance must share the device's public IP, because Cloudflare binds the clearance cookie to it. If FlareSolverr is unreachable, the app falls back to the built-in solver. #DNS over HTTPS Settings → Advanced → Networking → DNS over HTTPS. Twelve providers are available, from Cloudflare and Google to Quad9, AdGuard and others. DoH is applied to the app's OkHttp clients; the local Komga source deliberately uses the system DNS so IP-addressed servers keep working. A custom default user agent can be set, or reset to the current Chrome string. Changing it affects sites that key behaviour on the user agent; a reset is the first thing to try when a source starts behaving differently. #Cookies and WebView data Clear cookies — removes the app's HTTP cookie jar. Clear WebView data — clears the WebView profile used for logins and challenge solving. Clearing these logs you out of cookie-based sources and trackers. It does not delete your library or downloaded chapters. #Google Drive The Google Drive sync service uses OAuth. Sign in from Settings → Data and storage → Sync → Google Drive, then choose what to sync. See Backup & sync. Forks can register their own OAuth client with ; the default keeps existing credentials working. #SyncYomi and WebDAV These are library-sync services rather than "connections" in the social sense. Their setup, triggers, protocol v2 and conflict behaviour are covered in Backup & sync. #Network log levels Settings → Advanced → Log level controls diagnostics: Minimal (default) — warnings and errors in the in-memory ring; nothing written to disk. Verbose / Extra / Extreme — progressively more detail, including request and response headers. Extreme also captures the app's own networking (E-Hentai API, image loads, downloads, sync

title: Privacy & security
description: App lock, secure screen, incognito, encrypted databases and archives, and what leaves the device.
text: Hyoukan is local-first by default. It has no account, no advertising ID and no telemetry in the official release build. The privacy controls that do exist are about other people who can pick up your phone, and about the data you choose to send to services. #App lock Settings → Security → Require unlock. Option Behaviour Never No lock Always Ask every time the app comes to the foreground Lock when idle Ask after the app has been in the background for the configured time The lock uses the device's biometric or credential prompt. Additional controls: Lock times — choose the days and time ranges when the lock applies (for example, only at night). Biometric lock days — the same schedule expressed as days. Hide notification content — remove entry and chapter titles from notifications on the lock screen. The lock protects the app's UI. It does not encrypt the database; someone with root access or a full device backup can still read the files. See Database encryption below. #Secure screen Settings → Security → Secure screen. Mode Effect Always Hide app contents in the recents thumbnail and block screenshots everywhere Incognito Apply the same protection only while incognito mode is on Never Allow screenshots and recents previews Secure screen is implemented with Android's . It prevents screenshots and screen recording of the app, and blanks the recents card. It cannot stop a camera pointed at the screen. #Incognito mode More → Incognito (also available as a reader setting) stops the app from writing: history rows; reading progress; chapter read state; tracker progress updates. The current session still works; the position is held in memory. Incognito is a privacy mode for a session, not an access control, and turning it off does not retroactively record what you read. Some features intentionally keep working: downloads, translation and upscaling do not depend on history. Notifications and Discord presence can be configured to respect incognito. #Database encryption Settings → Advanced → Developer tools → Encrypt database. The database can be encrypted with SQLCipher. This is a destructive migration, not a toggle: Create a backup. Clear the app's data in Android settings. Open the app and enable Encrypt database. Force-restart the app. Restore the backup. The screen spells these steps out because enabling encryption on an existing database would otherwise create a new, empty database and strand the old file. The password is stored in the app's encrypted preference store; losing it means losing the database. Encryption protects the database file at rest. It does not encrypt downloaded images, logs or backups. #Encrypted downloads and archives Settings → Security → Password protect downloads encrypts downloaded CBZ archives. Setting Options Encryption type AES-256, AES-128 or standard ZipCrypto Set CBZ archive password The password used for new archives Delete CBZ archive password Remove the stored password Keys live in the Android KeyStore. Standard ZIP encryption is the most compatible and the least secure; AES-256 is the strongest. Warning If you forget the archive password, the data inside the archives is unrecoverable. There is no recovery key. Password protection applies to archives written after it is enabled. Existing downloads are not re-encrypted. #What leaves the device Destination What is sent When Sources / extensions Requests to the sites you browse, with the app's cookies and user agent Whenever you browse or read online Trackers Progress, scores, statuses and the account token When you track an entry or auto-sync Cloud LLM Page image or extracted text, depending on the provider Only if you select a cloud provider Ichigo image service Page image and a device fingerprint Only if you use it SyncYomi / WebDAV / Drive The sync payload you configure On sync Discord Presence and, if enabled, a webhook payload Only if enabled Webhooks The configured event payload Only for enabled events FlareSolverr The challenge request Only when enabled and needed Crashlytics Crash reports Only in builds compiled with telemetry There is no analytics SDK in the standard release. Logs stay in app-private storage until you share them. Source health diagnostics records failure counts in app-private preferences and never uploads them. The only way those records leave the device is the redacted report you choose to share; it carries source names and statuses, not library titles, URLs or reading history. #Permissions Hyoukan requests permissions only for features you use: Notifications — download, backup, update and library-update progress. Install and delete packages — extension installation and removal (the Private installer still needs no install permission). Query all packages — to list installed extensions on Android 11+. Storage — for the download/local-source tree, media-image read for custom covers, and legacy read/write on older Android versions. Network and Wi-Fi state — update and download restrictions. title: Troubleshooting
description: Diagnose the app without a computer — logs, crash reports, reader fallbacks, extension errors and sync failures.
headings: It falls back to the standard viewer
The screen is black, but pages are decoding
It opens at the wrong page
text: Most problems have one of four causes: an extension that has not caught up with its site, a network or Cloudflare block, a device-specific rendering limit, or a setting that is doing what it says. This page starts with the tools that tell you which one you are looking at. #First steps Update the app — About → Check for updates. Many reports describe bugs already fixed. Update the extension — a site change is the most common source failure. Restart the app — a force stop clears the source map and the reader state. Check the log — the app keeps a log ring even when nothing is written to disk. #Diagnostics #Log levels Settings → Advanced → Log level: Level What it records Where Minimal (default) Warnings and errors In-memory ring, flushed on demand Extra Adds debug detail and request/response headers File logging enabled Extreme Adds full network bodies for every app request File logging enabled; expensive Changing the level can affect performance and requires a force restart. Return to Minimal when you are done. #View logs Settings → Advanced → View logs browses the app's crash reports, dumps and logcat ring on-device. You can copy or share individual files. Clear logs wipes crash files, the ring and the system buffer. #Dump crash logs Settings → Advanced → Dump crash logs writes a shareable archive. It includes a short WebGPU session summary: what the reader decoded and how long it took; how tight memory was; whether pages were downsampled or evicted; whether a decode stalled; whether the GPU device was lost. A report with this attached is far more useful than "the reader is broken". Current builds count from frames the renderer actually presented, not from the reader's pre-submit flag; the summary also carries , and a line with the first drawn page's size, scale and mip count, plus the adapter backend and renderer/Dawn log lines. #Debug info Settings → Advanced → Debug info shows the version, build, device, ABI, memory class, database size and feature flags. Tapping the version row on About copies the same device-info block. #Worker info and backup schema The debug menu exposes scheduled workers and the backup schema. These are advanced tools; they are safe to inspect and copy, not to edit. #Source health diagnostics Settings → Advanced → Source health diagnostics shows which installed sources are answering. It is local-only: nothing is uploaded, and the screen reads connectivity only to decide whether a verdict is meaningful. Status Meaning Unknown No check has run, or the device is offline. Offline overrides every stored verdict and freezes the failure counts. Healthy The last call succeeded; the failure streak was cleared. Degraded The last call failed but the streak is under three — usually a transient timeout or HTTP error. Blocked A Cloudflare challenge or a login is in the way. One such failure is enough. Suspected dead Three DNS or 404 failures in a row. The site may have moved or closed. Failures are counted only while the device is online; a success clears the streak but keeps the lifetime total. Blocked wins over a long DNS/404 streak because the most recent failure kind is checked first. Refresh reloads the screen and Clear health records forgets every recorded failure. Export redacted report shares a plain-text summary through Android's share sheet: source names, statuses, failure counts, failure kinds and a success timestamp, never library titles, URLs, accounts or reading history. An offline export downgrades every status to Unknown so stale "dead" verdicts are not replayed. #App crashes The crash screen shows the full stack trace and device info, not just the exception name. A crash loop is tolerated for a burst of crashes before the app gives up, so a one-off crash does not lock you out. If the app will not start at all, the database may have failed its integrity check. The maintenance pass restores the latest daily database snapshot; if that fails, it quarantines the corrupt file as in app-private storage. If the database was reset, restore your latest backup. #Library and updates Symptom Likely cause What to do Library update finds nothing All entries skipped by rules Check Skip entries with unread chapters / unstarted / completed and category schedules A series never updates Excluded scanlator covers every chapter Open the chapter list → Scanlator filter Update errors list is empty but updates fail HTTP 401/404 only are recorded Check View logs at Extra level Entries missing after restore Restore was interrupted, or the backup was category-scoped Re-run the restore; check the source/tracker warnings Duplicate entries Same series from several sources Use Find duplicates and merge or migrate Covers not loading Coil cache or source blocked Long-press the cover to refresh; check the source in WebView Unread counts wrong Blacklisted chapters or merged entries Check the chapter blacklist and merge state #Sources and extensions Symptom Likely cause What to do Extension will not install Installe

title: Architecture
description: How the app is assembled — modules, dependency injection, navigation, package roots and the rules that keep the layers apart.
text: Hyoukan is a large Android application: roughly 2,300 files and 190,000 lines of Kotlin and Java. Every screen is a route implementing , rendered by the single in . Screens live in two places: — routes, screen composables and ViewModels; — the content composables. In-tab sub-navigation uses nested Nav3 back stacks inside an . #Activities outside Nav3 A few screens are deliberately activities: Activity Why The sole Nav3 host Fullscreen, , S-Pen remote, container transforms Login and challenge flows App lock OAuth login activities Tracker and Drive logins Trampoline to Nav3's The reader is not a Nav3 route and should not be migrated into one without a redesign; its lifecycle, orientation and input handling depend on being an activity. #Controller delegation State-heavy ViewModels hold state and thin intent methods; business logic lives in controllers beside them. title: Reader & WebGPU
description: The reader's activity model, page pipeline and the state machines behind the hardware renderer.
text: The reader is the largest and most failure-sensitive subsystem in the app. This page is the map for changing it: the entry points, the viewer contract, the page-loading path, and the WebGPU pipeline's threads, states, retries and memory rules. Note The WebGPU folder carries its own that is kept current by the people debugging it. This page summarises that knowledge; when the two disagree, the source and that file win. #Entry points File Role activity; AndroidX ViewModel holding chapter and page state / contracts, pager and webtoon viewers and the loaders , , , transitions , modes, orientation, settings models The hardware renderer's app-side half The book renderer (see Book engine) The activity is the only thing that knows when the reader stops, so declares three audience hooks, all default no-ops: / — fired from / . — fired from a for severe trim levels. Only WebGPU and the novel viewer implement them. The WebGPU viewer uses the first pair to park its memory monitor and the last to shed caches; the novel viewer drops its inlined-document and font-rule caches. The legacy viewers deliberately shed nothing: their only derived data is a next-chapter transition map that is content, not a cache. #Viewer selection asks each provider whether it claims a chapter. A from a provider means "not my kind of chapter", not "not this instance". claims a chapter whose loader is a — exactly what the registry picks for a . Image viewers decline text chapters explicitly ( ), so an EPUB can never reach a pager that would render it blank. If no provider claims a text chapter, throws rather than falling back silently. guards on , not on pages, because a text chapter has no image page list to inspect. The chosen renderer and whether the chapter was text are logged. description: The SQLDelight schema, migration rules, repository patterns and the streaming backup format.
text: All app state that is not a file lives in one SQLite database. This page covers the schema, the repository layer, the conventions that keep migrations safe, and how backups move that state between devices. #Schema SQLDelight sources live in : — tables and queries. — views. — schema migrations, currently through . There are 21 tables and 4 views. #Core tables Table Holds Library and non-library entries Chapter rows, read state, bookmarks, scanlator Entry ↔ category join Categories, flags, order, parent id Reading history Tracker links and scores Merge references between entries #Support tables Table Holds Known sources and their display data Saved source searches Feed definitions Per-entry scanlator exclusions Configured repositories , Update failures User-edited metadata Cached recommendations , , E-Hentai metadata , E-Hentai favourites #Views View Purpose Entry + aggregated chapter stats + categories, with a arm for the merged source Chapter updates with excluded-scanlator awareness History with max-read tracking and chapter counts Errors with entry metadata Views are where a schema change most often goes wrong: SQLDelight does not recreate a view when a table changes. A migration must drop and recreate the view body verbatim. #Migration rules Add a new ; never edit an applied one. Include every view whose body touches a changed column. Run after any / change. Add a test or a harness assertion for data-shape changes where possible. Keep preference key strings stable: backups match on raw keys, so renaming a preference needs a that rewrites the stored key. A JSON-encoded column cannot be matched by SQL text comparisons that assume the old encoding. The blacklist is the cautionary tale: and kept blacklisted chapters out of the badge and history totals with against a -joined string. When the blacklist moved to JSON, those predicates matched nothing and every blacklisted chapter was counted again. Both views now test both encodings, in all three arms. Any future encoding change needs the same treatment, and the migration must carry the recreated view. #Repositories There are 18 repository implementations in , each implementing a domain interface: and the smaller supporting repositories #Common patterns Coalesce updates — for partial DTOs. UPSERT — . Sync-aware versioning — triggers increment only when . Merged entries — views the synthetic source id . The library fetches the merged children of a whole page in one batched query for filtering, bulk download and bulk delete; one round trip per entry made large libraries of merged titles stall. #Custom metadata cache fronts with a process-wide cache because snapshots edits in a initializer. The cache exists to make an edited title/cover/description visible everywhere a snapshot is already held. #Preferences Preferences are 100% SharedPreferences — no DataStore. The framework lives in : Type Role Typed getters Reactive value with ; self-heals on type mismatch Production implementation Tests and previews Storage key + default, the single source of truth / Feature key contributions and duplicate detection Key prefixes: — excluded from backups unless the user opts in. — internal state, not user-facing. Source preferences are separate: each gets its own SharedPreferences file, outside the app store. Do not migrate them into s; the framework must never assume the default file. #Backup format A backup is a protobuf stream with a extension. It is written by and read by / . #Creation writes: metadata (counts, date, app version); categories; entries, with chapters, tracking, history and optionally custom covers; saved searches and feeds; extension stores; preferences (with always dropped, only when opted in). The file name is . #Restore The restore path is streaming: walks the entries by length to count them and hands back the stream. yields one at a time, skipping rejected entries by length. walks the protobuf by hand. The wire format is unchanged, so old and new backups are readable. An entry or metadata block whose declared length exceeds 64 MiB is refused, so a malformed length field cannot demand gigabytes of memory. is used only for the integrity check, which needs every entry's trackers; never call it on the restore path. Entries are classified as NEW / EXISTING / MERGED and the file is walked twice to realise the classification. Sorting would mean holding every entry in memory. takes a list and opens one transaction for the chunk, falling back to entry-by-entry if the batch throws. A large library used to do one transaction per entry — roughly 15,000 commits. The per-entry fetch-interval recompute reads the backup's own chapter list, not the table, because it runs before or independently of the rows just written. #Preferences in backups snapshots into typed values. type-switches them back and special-cases: category-id remapping; / category key sets; . text: Hyoukan's extension API is the Tachiyomi/Mihon API plus Hyoukan's text-source additions. Pages carry a status machine and a stream; the app handles loading, retries, splitting and caching. #ABI rules The extension API is a binary contract. These rules are not style preferences: Never add an abstract member to an existing interface. Extensions loaded through a classloader implement it; a new member breaks every extension that predates it, and R8 cannot see across the dex boundary to warn you. Add a new optional interface instead. Hosts check for it. exists for exactly this reason: can open an absolute URL, but only the source knows the base its relative references should resolve against. Adding a field to a model is safe; adding a parameter without a default is not. Models are data classes with defaults. Keep covering every class here. Extension APKs are compiled separately. The app's own interface is versioned by the metadata float; a source declares the API level it was built against, and the app refuses incompatible ones with an explanation. #Writing an image source A minimal HTTP source: The real API offers more: filters, paging, metadata, URL import, preferences. No timestamps, no array indexes. Self-contained — the host hands it straight to a WebView. description: Add a setting or a screen without breaking search, backups, tablets or translations.
headings: Never rename a key without a migration
text: Settings are not hand-built rows. A modular framework wires a storage key to a UI row, so a preference has one source of truth and every screen can be searched. This page is the procedure and the traps. #The layers Piece Location Role ( ) Exact storage key + default object Beside each class All keys one feature owns Key + title + store binding + row builder Beside the settings screen The feature's definition list; self-registers for duplicate detection / Definitions → through the existing dispatcher Base class for definition-driven screens; still searchable The single searchable-screen list The renderer is still . Framework rows look and behave exactly like hand-built ones. Non-standard rows (navigation, async data, login widgets) remain hand-built as escape hatches. A second, unrelated system exists in : ( , , , , …). It is used by non-settings screens (library sort, source filters, the reader's appearance sheet) and takes raw objects. Do not confuse the two. Unify them only deliberately — they serve different hosts. #Adding a setting Three steps: Add the key to the feature's object. Apply / here, not at call sites. Add one definition to the feature's host: , , , or . Render it by including it in the host list consumed by / . Keep the accessor as a thin delegate over the same key. Screens, backup ( keys) and DI ( ) depend on it. #Never rename a key without a migration Backups match raw key strings. A rename needs a that rewrites the stored value, or restored libraries silently lose the setting. #Adding a screen Create a screen extending (or directly if most rows are custom). Build its groups from host definitions. Register it in both (the search index) and (the hub icon and subtitle). Missing either list breaks something silently: the screen is unreachable, or unsearchable. There is no compile-time check. #Search The settings hub has a search row. The index covers every registered screen — Discord, webhooks, achievements, the MTL sub-screens and the launcher identity screen included. It matches screen titles, group headings, row titles and summaries, searches all words in any order ("black theme" finds the AMOLED switch), and does not stop at ten results. #Parity rules Regressions live here: / / helpers default their subtitle to (the value preview), matching the hand-built data-class defaults. Do not "clean up" that fallback. uses a plain loop. builders cannot be called inside . Keep item order identical to the screen being migrated; search matches on title text. The framework must never assume the default SharedPreferences file. Source preferences ( ) are outside it by design. #Tablet two-pane navigation On a tablet, the settings hub is the left pane and the top back-stack entry is the right one ( in ). The hub's row handler in pops everything above the hub and then opens the row. Replacing only the top entry stranded the previous section in the stack, and the duplicate guard then matched the route being returned to, making the row a dead tap until the user left settings entirely. Any new settings entry point must go through that helper. Adding rows with a bare reintroduces the dead row. #Backup interaction snapshots . Accessor delegates to the key. Host definition added. Row rendered. Backup behaviour considered (private? category id?). Strings in if Hyoukan-only. Search finds it by title and summary. description: Unit tests, the offline Kotlin harnesses and the conventions a change must satisfy before CI accepts it.
headings: The rule that makes them possible
text: Hyoukan's test strategy is unusual: a small set of unit tests, plus a large set of offline harnesses that compile the real project sources with a cached Kotlin compiler and assert pure policy. The harnesses exist because much of the risky logic — reader state, memory budgets, EPUB parsing — can be made Android-free and tested in a second. #Unit tests There are 22 test files across three modules: Module Count Notes 11 Interactors, search parsing, fetch intervals 10 Includes 1 Engine helper logic , presentation and core modules have no unit tests. There are no tests and no Robolectric. #Frameworks JUnit Jupiter 6 Kotest assertions ( ) MockK ( , , ) ( ) Each tested module opts in with plus . #Conventions on every class. Backtick test names that read as sentences. model factories. for suspend work. Assertions with Kotest, mocks with MockK. #The offline Kotlin check compiles changed Kotlin files without Gradle: It drives straight from the Gradle dependency cache, so it needs no network, Android SDK or Compose plugin, and finishes in about a second. Dependencies that are not cached (jsoup, libarchive) and platform classes that do not exist off-device ( , ) are satisfied by deliberate stubs in , never compiled into the app. What it catches: syntax errors; JVM declaration clashes (a colliding with a property); intra-module type errors; anything a pure function can be asserted against. It also catches the nested-KDoc trap: Kotlin block comments nest, so a written inside a KDoc opens a second comment; the file's final closes that one, and the outer comment runs to EOF and silently swallows every declaration after it. Never write inside a doc comment, even backticked. What it is not: a build. Unresolved references are suppressed and counted, because most come from the absent classpath. It runs neither Spotless nor ktlint. #Harnesses is the behavioural half. Each links the real project source (never a copy) and prints / per case. At the time of writing there are 19 harnesses covering: Area Examples Archive / EPUB path resolution, OPF metadata, document construction Novel reader typography, progress, plain-text conversion, footnotes WebGPU decode priority, stuck ladder, spread geometry, memory budget, image headers, EXIF rotation, preload guard, continuous column width, session diagnostics Translation page validation, encoding, prompt parsing, status Upscaling planning, identity, fallbacks Library search parsing, fetch intervals #The rule that makes them possible Policy that decides something a user can see belongs in a file with no Android import. That is why , , , , , and are pure. A harness can reach them; a device is not required. When you change a decision a user can see, extract the policy and add a harness case. Do not assert on a copy of the algorithm. #Formatting Spotless + ktlint, configured in . is a CI gate. A change is not done until it passes. If it fails, run and re-check. #Conventions #Logging Hyoukan code: / from . Mihon code: from . Never raw . #Strings Kind Module Class Hyoukan-only Shared upstream TachiyomiSY-only Only locale files are edited; Weblate owns the rest. A Hyoukan string in is a review failure. #Fork markers Preserve and use: New Hyoukan-only code goes in islands. Marker islands move whole; never cut one open. #Release notes Add a user-facing bullet to for anything a user could notice. Skip pure refactors, tests and CI. Use , or . #Migrations A schema change needs a new , any affected views recreated verbatim, and . A preference rename needs a . A backup-format change needs backward-compatible defaults. #Review checklist The change is in the right layer (UI / domain / data / source API). New Hyoukan code is inside markers. Strings use . A new setting has a key, host definition and row. A new settings screen is registered in both lists. A schema change has a migration and regenerated interface. A preference rename has a migration. A user-visible change has a release note. Policy is Android-free and covered by a harness where practical. passes. Both flavours compile. The extension ABI is unchanged, or the change is additive and optional. #Why this matters The app ships to devices the maintainers do not own. The harnesses and the offline compiler check are how a change gets meaningful feedback without a full Gradle build or a physical phone. They are not a substitute for a build, but they catch the mistakes that would otherwise only appear in CI or in a field report.

title: Files & formats
description: Backup schema, local-source layout, extension indexes, download trees and the formats the decoder accepts.
text: #Backups ( ) A backup is a protobuf stream. The top-level message carries: Field Contents Library and read entries Categories, including parent ids History rows Typed preference values Repository URLs Saved source searches Feed definitions Merge relationships User-edited metadata , , E-Hentai caches E-Hentai favourites , , counts Metadata A contains the entry's URL, title, cover, metadata, chapters, tracking rows, history, categories, custom cover bytes and merge references. A contains the URL, name, scanlator, read/bookmark state, last page and date. The format is intentionally stable: old and new backups are both readable because the reader walks the protobuf by field length rather than materialising it. Warning A backup is not a database file. Do not rename a to , and do not try to open it with SQLite. #Local source The local source reads a folder you choose. Each immediate subfolder is an entry; each file or subfolder inside it is a chapter. Rules: Supported image files become pages, sorted naturally by name. , , are recognised as the cover. is read when present. is read for title, series, volume, summary, writer, artist and publishing status. Hidden folders are ignored unless the setting is enabled. A folder whose chapters are all books ( , , ) is a book series; a mixed folder is a comic. An EPUB can also be read as an image chapter if the entry is explicitly set to comic. A single , or file can stand as its own local-source entry. Files imported through Settings → Book reading → Import books are copied into one new local-source folder and matched by file name, case-insensitively; the MIME type is ignored. # accepts , , , , or . # ComicInfo is the ComicRack schema. Hyoukan reads the common fields ( , , , , , , , , , , , , , ). It is also written into encrypted archives with random padding as an anti-fingerprint measure. #FB2 and TXT conversion FB2 is parsed as XML: each leaf becomes a reader section, with as its heading. Emphasis, strong, strikethrough, sub/superscript, code, citation, epigraphs, annotations and verse lines map to HTML with inline CSS; images are not inlined and only links are kept. Encoding is taken from a byte-order mark or an declaration, falling back to UTF-8. TXT is normalised to line feeds, split into paragraphs on blank lines (single newlines become ), escaped, and packed into sections of at most 12,000 characters, preferring paragraph boundaries and falling back to sentence or hard cuts inside an over-long paragraph. Both conversions run entirely on the device. Parsed sections are cached per chapter and files over 64 MiB are refused. Search in chapter uses a case-insensitive literal index with context snippets. FB2/TXT files keep the generated placeholder cover. Note FB2 and TXT support is on the current build, not in the stable 1.25.3 release. The Import books strings still say "EPUB" even though the picker accepts all three formats. #Downloads Downloads live under the chosen storage location: output is optional. Include chapter URL hash appends the first six characters of the chapter URL's MD5 to the chapter folder or file name. Disallow non-ASCII filenames affects source and entry folder names; chapter files are not renamed. A book chapter stores the source EPUB as ; it is never wrapped in a CBZ. #Supported archives Format Reading Writing ZIP / CBZ Yes Yes RAR / CBR Yes No 7z Yes No EPUB Yes (book or comic) No Encrypted CBZ AES-256, AES-128, ZipCrypto AES-256, AES-128, ZipCrypto Archive reading uses libarchive through JNI with memory-mapped files. #Supported image formats The libvips decoder handles: JPEG · PNG · WebP · GIF · AVIF · HEIF · JPEG XL (JXL) · JPEG 2000 (JP2) · TIFF Animated GIF, animated WebP and animated HEIF are recognised as animated where the platform supports them. HDR variants (PQ, HLG, UltraHDR) are supported by the WebGPU reader; the legacy viewer tone-maps or clamps them. Crop borders are applied after decode; the decoder itself has no native trim. #EPUB expectations Hyoukan reads: EPUB 2 with ; EPUB 3 with (only a nav marked ); OPF metadata in any namespace binding; for DRM and font obfuscation; percent-encoded and non-ASCII file names; charset declarations from the XML prolog; Calibre and EPUB 3 series metadata. It does not read: DRM-protected content (it reports the book as locked); resources hosted outside the archive; EPUBs with a spine entry missing from the manifest (that entry is dropped). #Extension repository index A repository publishes a JSON index. The modern format is an array: The app also accepts a legacy format with a store object ( , , , ) and a separate extension list. The store base URL resolves and . The signing key is the trust anchor: the Private installer verifies the downloaded APK against it before storing. Remote store indexes and extension lists are capped at 16 MiB; a larger response is refused with a clear error before it is buffered. #Sync payload SyncYomi, WebDAV and Google Drive carry the same protobuf payload as a backu

title: Glossary
description: The vocabulary used across Hyoukan, its documentation and its code.
text: #A–C Term Meaning ABI The CPU instruction set an APK targets: , , , . Extensions and native features depend on it. Achievement An optional collectible milestone. Positive, secret, negative or rotating. Activity An Android screen with its own lifecycle. The reader and main UI are activities; most other screens are Navigation 3 routes. AdaptiveSheet A Compose bottom sheet that adapts to phone/tablet layouts. Used for dialogs inside tabs. Archive A container of pages: ZIP/CBZ, RAR/CBR, 7z, EPUB. Read through libarchive. AST search The library's field-aware query syntax ( , , , quotes). Toggleable. Auto webtoon Automatically using the continuous viewer for entries whose pages look like a long strip. Backup A protobuf snapshot of library data and selected settings. Beta A minified preview build published from every push as . Blacklist (chapter) A per-entry list of chapters hidden from the chapter list and update counts. Book A text entry rendered by the novel viewer, usually an EPUB. Contrast Comic. Catalogue A source's browse/search listing of entries. Category A library label. Can contain subcategories. CBZ A ZIP archive of images, optionally encrypted. Chapter A unit inside an entry. An image chapter has pages; a book chapter has text documents. Chapter cache Pages cached while reading, evictable and separate from downloads. Cloudflare challenge A bot check in front of a site; solved by a WebView, FlareSolverr or a visible Turnstile popup. ComicInfo.xml The ComicRack metadata file read from local folders and archives. Compose Jetpack Compose, the UI toolkit used for all app screens. ConfigurableSource A source with its own preferences in . Continuous vertical A long-strip reading mode. Cover-based theme A palette derived from the open entry's cover. #D–H Term Meaning DB (database) The SQLite database holding entries, chapters, categories, history and tracking. Delegated source An installed extension served by an in-app implementation (notably Komga). DoH DNS over HTTPS. Twelve providers are selectable. Download An explicitly saved chapter, kept until deleted. Contrast chapter cache. Dual page Two pages side by side, with height matching. Enhanced tracker A tracker discovered from a server (Kavita, Komga, Suwayomi) rather than logged into. Entry A series, book or one-shot in the library or in a source. EPUB An open ebook format: OPF package, spine documents, resources and a TOC. Extension A separately installed APK that provides one or more sources. Extension store A repository index of extensions, with a signing key for verification. Feed A multi-source stream of latest entries and saved searches. FlareSolverr An external Cloudflare-solving service the app can use. Force dark A palette rewrite for books, not a colour filter. Global search A search across every enabled source. GPU device The Vulkan/WebGPU device used by the hardware reader. A lost device triggers recovery. HDR High dynamic range pages (PQ, HLG, UltraHDR), rendered at full brightness by WebGPU. Hyoukan This app. Formerly Houri, and before that a Komikku fork. #I–M Term Meaning Incognito A session mode that writes no history or progress. Installer (extension) Private, Shizuku, Legacy or Package installer. Interactor A domain use case ( , ). JXL JPEG XL, a modern image format the decoder supports. Komga A self-hosted comic/manga/ebook server, supported as a built-in source and tracker. Library The set of entries you saved, plus their organisation. Library update A scheduled refresh that fetches new chapters and metadata. Local source The built-in source that reads folders, archives and EPUBs on the device. Long strip A continuous vertical reading mode (webtoon). LUT Look-up table for colour grading. Presets and custom / files. Merge Combining several source entries into one library entry. Metro The dependency-injection framework used by the app. Migration Moving an entry to another source, or a database schema change ( ). Mihon The upstream reader Hyoukan ultimately derives from, alongside TachiyomiSY. Moko resources The string-resource system ( , , ). MTL Machine translation — the page-translation pipeline. MangaBaka A tracker with full progress sync. #N–R Term Meaning Navigation 3 AndroidX's navigation library; every screen is a serializable route. Negative achievement A "shame" achievement that does not count toward rank. NCNN A neural-network inference framework used by the upscaler and the translation detector/inpainter. Nomtl The build flavour without the translation engine. Novel viewer The WebView-based book renderer. ONNX An open model format; used by OCR, the NPU upscaler and imported models. OPF The EPUB package document ( ) listing metadata, manifest and spine. Page An image unit with a load state and a stream. Page split Cutting a too-tall page into segments that replace it in the page list. Preference A persisted setting ( / ). Private installer The extension installer that needs no install permission and verifies signatures. Provid

title: Project history
description: From Tachiyomi to Mihon, TachiyomiSY, Komikku and Houri — where Hyoukan comes from and what each layer contributed.
text: Hyoukan is the current name of a fork with a long lineage. Understanding that lineage explains why the codebase contains several package roots, three string modules and inline / markers. #Timeline Period Project What happened 2015–2024 Tachiyomi The original open-source Android manga reader, created by Javier Tomás. Apache-2.0. 2024 Mihon The community continuation after Tachiyomi was discontinued. Modern maintenance, Navigation 3, the current image decoder and many backports. 2020s TachiyomiSY A long-running fork adding the Feed, automatic webtoon detection, lewd filtering, custom source categories, merging, migration and more. 2020s Komikku A fork of TachiyomiSY/Mihon with a large feature set: library improvements, trackers, translation, WebGPU work and more. 2026 Houri The development name of this fork while it was being rebuilt around Komikku. 2026 Hyoukan The published name. The repository, update channels and documentation use it. The exact branch points are less important than the practical consequence: Hyoukan carries the entire Mihon and TachiyomiSY feature set, plus Komikku's additions, plus its own work. #What each layer contributed #Tachiyomi The original architecture and vocabulary: sources as installable extensions; the library, chapters, categories, history and tracking model; the reader with pager and webtoon modes; the extension API that every fork still honours. Tachiyomi's package root ( ) is still the app's namespace. #Mihon The modern maintenance line: current AndroidX and Compose versions; Navigation 3 migration; the upstream image decoder; database schema reworks and performance work; a steady stream of reader and library fixes. Hyoukan's package root marks this layer. #TachiyomiSY The feature-heavy fork: the Feed tab; automatic webtoon detection; the lewd filter and NSFW controls; custom source categories; merging, migration and duplicate handling; enhanced E-Hentai features; archive encryption. The package root and strings mark this layer. #Komikku The immediate parent of this fork's feature set: library subcategories, smart categories and per-category settings; additional trackers (MangaBaka, Anime-Planet, ComicK, Hikka); the WebGPU reader work; AI translation and upscaling; book/EPUB reading; achievements, webhooks and Discord RPC; the modular settings framework. The markers and strings mark this layer. #Houri → Hyoukan The current fork's own work: the reader and WebGPU pipeline hardening; EPUB and novel-reader completion (paged, double, highlights, TTS, footnotes, custom CSS/JS); the upscaling pipeline rewrite; the translation spine rewrite; app identity and launcher personalisation; expanded diagnostics and log viewer; SyncYomi protocol v2; the settings search and tablet two-pane fixes; the wiki you are reading. #The name The project was developed and published as Houri while the fork was being rebuilt. It was renamed Hyoukan when the repository and update channels moved. The rename is deliberately conservative: the Android application ID remains ; the database name, backup file prefix and several preference keys still say or ; the beta repository and APK asset names may still carry legacy spellings; a few strings still mention Houri. These are compatibility identifiers, not a second product. Changing them would break upgrades, backups and existing library databases. The product, the documentation and the public repository use Hyoukan. #Licence and credits Hyoukan is licensed under Apache-2.0, inherited from Tachiyomi. The original copyright notice (Javier Tomás, 2015) is preserved in . The project exists because of: the Tachiyomi, Mihon, TachiyomiSY and Komikku maintainers and contributors; the extension developers who keep sources working; the translators on Weblate; everyone who files a reproducible bug report. The app hosts zero content. Its developers have no affiliation with any content provider. #Where to go next Versions & channels — the release history and channel rules. Architecture — how the layers are arranged today. Contributing — how to add to the lineage.

title: Contributing
description: Report bugs, translate, write code, or improve this wiki — and know which rules CI enforces.
headings: The rules that get PRs rejected
text: Hyoukan is a volunteer project. Contributions are welcome in several forms, and the most useful ones are not always code. #Report a bug Update the app and the extension first. Search the existing issues and the changelog. Open a new issue with: app version and build number (About); device, Android version and ABI; steps to reproduce; expected vs actual behaviour; a log dump from Settings → Advanced → Dump crash logs; a screenshot if it is visual. Do not group unrelated problems into one issue. A reproducible report with a log is worth more than a long one without. For extension bugs, use the extension's own repository. Hyoukan cannot fix a source it does not own; the Extensions screen builds the GitHub search link for you. #Request a feature Open an issue describing: what you want to do; why the current behaviour does not let you do it; how you imagine it working; any prior art (another reader, a fork, a website). For a major change, discuss it before writing code. A design that conflicts with the app's structure is expensive to discover after implementation. #Translate Translations are managed on Weblate. The app links to the project from About → Help translate. Rules: only edit locale files in a pull request; never edit non-base or in , or ; use for Hyoukan-only strings, for shared upstream strings, for TachiyomiSY strings; keep placeholders ( , ) intact. CI path-filters non-base locales, so a translation-only PR is handled by Weblate, not by code review. #Contribute code #Before you start Read the repository's and the guide for the module you are touching: Area Guide App module, screens, DI Reader WebGPU Domain Data / SQLDelight Source API Archive / EPUB Settings framework Trackers E-Hentai Upscaling Translation Native LLM These files are maps, not suggestions. They record invariants that have already cost incidents. #Setup The first build downloads dependencies and native tools. needs the WSL setup on Windows; see Build & release. #Branch and commit External contributions: use a feature branch and open a pull request. Agent-assisted sessions in this repository follow : work on , do not create a branch, commit or run Gradle unless the user asks. Keep commits focused. One concern per commit is easier to review and revert. When porting an upstream PR, co-author its author in the commit trailer. #What CI enforces Gate Rule Formatting (ktlint) Unit tests Both flavours and compile Path filters Non-base locale changes are ignored Release notes A user-visible change needs a bullet in #The rules that get PRs rejected Adding a Hyoukan-only string to instead of . Renaming a preference key without a migration. Changing a schema without a and regenerated interface. Breaking the extension ABI by adding an abstract member. Writing policy with Android imports where a harness could reach it. Cutting a or island open. Skipping . A user-visible change with no release note. #Improve this wiki The wiki source lives in in the site repository. Every page has an Edit this page link at the bottom. The generator reads , renders Markdown with the vendored build, and writes . It has no runtime dependencies and needs no network. When editing: keep the frontmatter ( , ); use relative links between pages — the builder rewrites them; use the callout syntax: run the builder and check the page before committing; keep claims verifiable. If a behaviour is version-specific, say so. #Code of conduct Be civil. Assume good faith. Disagreement about code is fine; personal attacks are not. The project follows the spirit of the Contributor Covenant in . #Where help is most useful Reproducible bug reports with logs. Extension maintenance (separate repositories). Translations. Documentation: this wiki, module guides, troubleshooting notes. Reader testing on unusual devices: e-ink, foldables, low-RAM phones, 32-bit devices, unusual GPUs. Regression tests and harnesses for policy that currently has none. #Thank you Every bug report that includes a log, every translated string and every harness case makes the next release a little less mysterious. That is the whole contribution model.
